title: Solar Open 2 Technical Report
data_curation: Pre-training: an initially cleaned 20T-token pool is refined to a 10T mixture; every dataset gets an in-house quality score and rarity is tracked by source/type, with exact and semantic dedup and a domain/language/source taxonomy. Ablation-tuned mixture: real:synthetic 4:6, math and code each >=15%, English >80%. Post-training data comes from purpose-built agent scenarios, each admitted only after execution- or evidence-based verification and decontaminated against eval benchmarks: MCP tool tasks with verifier-first CUD synthesis (sandboxed pytest read-back checks) and a live policy-bound transactional DB with a user simulator; SWE environments from PRs in 18 languages kept only if the LLM-synthesized Docker env builds and is fail-to-pass, Git history stripped, trajectories from 5 scaffolds (OpenHands, Claude Code, OpenCode, KiloCode, HermesAgent) filtered by a 5-dimension judge rubric and repo-level decontamination; terminal tasks across 10+ domains stressing self-tests; front-end artifacts over 6 categories filtered by Playwright plus VLM-judged screenshots; and OfficeVerse, an 11-industry x 12-task-type office-task synthesizer grounded in public data, with weighted rubrics and a Korean office-work track.
curriculum: Pre-training has four stages: (1) selective weight transfer from Solar Open 1, (2) General Pre-training on 10T tokens, (3) Intensive Pre-training on the best 1T tokens re-filtered at a higher quality threshold, (4) Length Expansion (~0.9T/865B tokens) to 1M context with long documents, repo-level code, and injected reasoning/agent data; four intermediate checkpoints are merged to offset a Stage-4 performance drop (final merge scores 0.745 on a 50+-metric PLM average). Post-training has four stages: SFT covering reasoning and agent tasks, Multi-domain RL with verifiable rewards on STEM-centered tasks, a Specialist stage training twelve domain teachers (SFT + domain RL) in parallel, and Multi-teacher On-Policy Distillation (MOPD) consolidating them into one model. Office tasks use an expertise curriculum that progressively strips scaffolding from prompts.
method: 250B-A15B MoE (48 layers, hidden 4,096, 320 routed + 1 shared expert, top-8, 196,608-token Korean-efficient vocab) with a hybrid S-L-L-L stack: 12 GQA softmax layers with a sigmoid output gate and 36 KDA linear layers with negative eigenvalues (beta in (0,2)), and no positional encoding, giving 1M context. Selective weight transfer reuses 5.69B (~2.3%) shape-compatible parameters from Solar Open 1 (embeddings, norms, GQA q/k/v/o, linear q/o, shared expert); routed experts are random. Fully asynchronous RL: disaggregated trainer/actor with in-flight weight updates and KV recompute, a fresh-token-fraction gateway (per-token staleness <= s_max; trajectories admitted if fresh ratio >= rho, stale prefix masked), length-binned stalest-first batch sampling, direct double-sided token-level importance sampling, and environment-failure filtering with GRPO group-size repair. MOPD routes each prompt to one of twelve teachers and minimizes exact full-vocabulary per-position reverse KL on student rollouts, with no outcome reward and one rollout per prompt; the teacher ships pre-lm_head hidden states and the student rebuilds logits in 1,024-token tiles.
eval_metrics: English: MMLU-Pro, GPQA-Diamond, HLE (no tools), LiveCodeBench v6, ArtifactsBench, HMMT2602, AIME2026, MultiChallenge, IFBench, AA-LCR, SWE-Bench Verified, Terminal Bench Hard, APEX-Agents, MCP-Atlas, tau3 banking, GDPval-AA v2 (ELO). Korean: KMMLU-Pro, CLIcK, HAE-RAE v1.1, Ko-AIME'25, HRM8K, KBank-MMLU, KBL, KorMedMCQA, and Ko-GDPval (in-house, 170 tasks, 58 occupations, 11 domains). Solar Open 2 posts MMLU-Pro 86.2, LiveCodeBench 92.4, GPQA-D 86.3, AIME2026 95.7, SWE-Bench Verified 70.4, Terminal Bench Hard 28.3, APEX-Agents 16.6, MCP-Atlas 58.2, GDPval-AA 1128; Korean average 85.4, Ko-GDPval 86.8. A blind pairwise test on 835 Korean turns prefers it over DeepSeek-V4-Flash 44.1% vs 26.6%. Baselines are DeepSeek-V4-Flash, MiMo-V2.5, Command A+, Mistral Medium 3.5, Solar Open 1, plus Claude Haiku 4.5 and GPT-5.4 mini on Korean.
key_results: Solar Open 2 leads comparably sized open-weight models on MMLU-Pro (86.2), LiveCodeBench v6 (92.4) and APEX-Agents (16.6), posts the top Korean average (85.4 vs DeepSeek-V4-Flash 84.9 and GPT-5.4 mini 80.8), and scores 86.8 on Ko-GDPval vs 86.9 for the 1.6T DeepSeek-V4-Pro (Solar Open 1: 3.4). Gaps remain on SWE-Bench Verified (70.4 vs 73.0-73.8) and Terminal Bench Hard (28.3 vs MiMo-V2.5's 41.7).
evolution_note: Solar Open 2 scales Upstage's Solar Open 1 (102B-A12B) into a Korean sovereign agentic model. It adopts the 2025-26 hybrid linear/softmax attention trend (Kimi Linear, Qwen3.5, Nemotron 3) and adds NoPE and negative eigenvalues. It also follows the specialist-then-on-policy-distillation consolidation used by DeepSeek-V4, Nemotron and MiMo, but drops the outcome reward and uses exact full-vocabulary KL. Its selective cross-architecture weight transfer and OfficeVerse office-task synthesis are reusable ideas for continuing model families across architecture changes and for training deliverable-producing agents in non-English languages.
